2027-03-14.title: Sixth Sunday of the Great Fast
2027-03-14.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The Lord gave Israel the land he promised
Do not be a stumbling block to your brother
The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep
2027-03-14.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). The last Sunday before Hosanna Sunday; this week brings the Fortieth Friday.
2027-03-14.verse: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
theo: “When morning dawned, the angels urged Lot, saying, ‘Get up, take your wife and your two daughters who are here, or else you will be consumed in the punishment of the city.’” The prophet Ezekiel would later name the sin of Sodom as pride, excess of food, prosperous ease, and neglect of the poor and needy (Ezekiel 16:49), and Genesis has just shown its violence against strangers. Lot knows the city is doomed, and still: “But he lingered.” It is one of the most human sentences in the Bible. We too linger at the door of conversion, knowing what we must leave and not quite leaving it. And then mercy acts: “so the men seized him and his wife and his two daughters by the hand, the LORD being merciful to him, and they brought him out and left him outside the city.” God does not wait for Lot to be brave; he takes him by the hand. Genesis adds that God did this because “God remembered Abraham” (Genesis 19:29), whose bold prayer for the city comes just before this story (Genesis 18:23–32). The command is urgent: “Flee for your life; do not look back or stop anywhere in the Plain.” Lot bargains even now for a small town nearby, and God grants it. “But Lot's wife, behind him, looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.” She was out of the city, but her heart was still in it. Jesus gave his disciples a sermon of three words on her: “Remember Lot's wife” (Luke 17:32). One week before Hosanna Sunday, the Great Fast takes us by the hand and says: do not look back, do not stop on the plain; the hills of Easter are ahead.

The second reading closes the long account of the conquest with a sentence of pure gratitude: “Thus the LORD gave to Israel all the land that he swore to their ancestors that he would give them.” And then: “Not one of all the good promises that the LORD had made to the house of Israel had failed; all came to pass.” Joshua sends the tribes who had settled east of the Jordan back to their homes, but not without a charge: “to love the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commandments, and to hold fast to him, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul.” The promised land is not the end of the covenant but a place to keep it. Paul then turns to a quarrel in the church of Rome. Some believers ate everything; others, out of conscience, would not eat meat or drink wine; each side judged the other. Paul tells the strong: “Let us therefore no longer pass judgment on one another, but resolve instead never to put a stumbling block or hindrance in the way of another.” And he gives a principle that every Lent needs: “For the kingdom of God is not food and drink but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.” Our families keep the Great Fast in different ways, from the strict fifty days of our grandparents to the lighter practice of busy young people abroad; the measure is not whose plate is emptier but whose heart is more loving. And Paul's warning reaches further: “it is good not to eat meat or drink wine or do anything that makes your brother or sister stumble.” Many families in Kerala have been wounded by drink. A father who gives up alcohol for the sake of his son, or a host who serves no liquor at a feast for the sake of one guest who struggles, is doing exactly what Paul asks: “Do not let what you eat cause the ruin of one for whom Christ died.”

In the Gospel Jesus speaks the words that the Church loves to hear at the threshold of his Passion: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.” He contrasts himself with the hired hand who “sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep and runs away,” because “a hired hand does not care for the sheep.” A shepherd is known by what he does when danger comes. Then he speaks of a knowledge as deep as the life of God: “I know my own and my own know me, just as the Father knows me and I know the Father. And I lay down my life for the sheep.” His gaze goes beyond the flock in front of him: “I have other sheep that do not belong to this fold. I must bring them also, and they will listen to my voice. So there will be one flock, one shepherd.” The St Thomas Christians, one Church for many centuries, have been divided into several Churches since the seventeenth century; we pray with respect and hope for the day when all will be one flock. Finally Jesus says what makes the coming week intelligible: “No one takes it from me, but I lay it down of my own accord. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it up again.” The Passion we will celebrate is not an accident or a defeat; it is the free self-offering of the Son, who lays down his life in order to take it up again. Every bishop of our Church carries a shepherd's staff, and every priest stands at the altar to make present that one sacrifice. Let us pray for our shepherds, that they may not be hired hands, and let us listen this week for the voice of the Good Shepherd, who is already walking toward Jerusalem for us.
conn: Jesus warns, “Remember Lot's wife” (Luke 17:32), and teaches that “No one who puts a hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God” (Luke 9:62).

Abraham interceded for Sodom (Genesis 18:23–32), and “God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow” (Genesis 19:29). The prayer of the just reaches those who cannot pray for themselves.
Joshua's words, not one good promise failed (Joshua 21:45; 23:14), find their fullness in Christ, in whom “every one of God's promises is a ‘Yes’” (2 Corinthians 1:20).
Joshua's charge to love the LORD and serve him with all your heart and soul (Joshua 22:5) repeats the great commandment of Deuteronomy 6:5, which Jesus called the first of all (Mark 12:29–30).
Paul makes the same choice in Corinth: “if food is a cause of their falling, I will never eat meat” (1 Corinthians 8:13); Jesus warns those who cause a little one to stumble (Matthew 18:6).

The LORD is my shepherd (Psalm 23:1); God promises to seek his scattered sheep himself (Ezekiel 34:11–16); Christ is “the shepherd and guardian of your souls” (1 Peter 2:25) and “the great shepherd of the sheep” (Hebrews 13:20).
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Good Shepherd lays down his life for the sheep: the one sacrifice of the Cross is made present on the altar, and he who laid down his life and took it up again feeds his flock with his own Body and Blood.

Around the altar the many sheep become one flock: those who keep the fast strictly and those who keep it lightly, the strong and the weak, receive the same Bread, and none may be a stumbling block to another.
outline: Ask: where am I lingering at the door, or looking back?
Mercy that takes us by the hand.
Holding fast in the land of promise.
No stumbling block for a brother or sister.
He lays down his life of his own accord.
A woman turned to salt on the road out of the burning plain, and a shepherd walking ahead of his flock toward Jerusalem.
“The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.”
live: Name the one thing you keep looking back at, a habit, a resentment, a relationship, and make a definite break with it before Hosanna Sunday.
Write down three promises God has kept in your family's life, and read them aloud at the family prayer.
Give up for the rest of the fast one thing, a drink, a habit of speech, a way of using the phone, that may lead someone close to you into sin.
Pray each day this week for your bishop and parish priest, and for vocations to the priesthood from your parish.
fathers: The hireling does not always flee by running away; he flees when he sees the wolf and keeps silent. He flees in his heart when he will not stand up for the sheep, because he loves his own comfort more than the flock.

Christ did not refuse to die for your brother, and will you not give up a dish of food for him? He gave his life; you are asked only to deny yourself a little meat or wine so that the one for whom he died may not fall.
magis: By embracing in his human heart the Father's love for men, Jesus loved them to the end; his suffering and death were the free offering of his life: no one takes it from me, but I lay it down of my own accord.
The Church is a sheepfold whose one gate is Christ, and a flock of which God himself foretold that he would be the shepherd.
Scandal is an attitude or behaviour which leads another to do evil; it is a grave offence when by deed or omission another is deliberately led into sin.
Hope is the virtue by which we desire the kingdom of heaven and eternal life, placing our trust in Christ's promises and relying on the help of the Holy Spirit.
The seasons and days of penance, especially Lent and each Friday in memory of the Lord's death, are intense moments of the Church's penitential practice.
saints: 15–20 Mar: sixth week of the Great Fast. 19 Mar: Sixth Friday of the Great Fast, the Fortieth Friday (Nalpatham Velli), with St Joseph, Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary. 20 Mar: the Saturday before Hosanna, recalling Lazarus and the anointing at Bethany; kozhukatta are made in many homes. 21 Mar: Hosanna Sunday.
2027-03-14.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Good Shepherd, you lay down your life for the sheep of your own accord, and you take it up again. When we linger at the door of conversion, take us by the hand as the angels took Lot, and do not let us look back. Keep us faithful to your promises, every one of which is Yes in you. Make us careful never to place a stumbling block before those for whom you died, and gather all your scattered sheep into one flock under your one staff. As you walk toward Jerusalem, let us hear your voice and follow you. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.

quick: Lot lingered, and God's mercy took him by the hand; his wife looked back and was lost.
Not one of God's promises failed; Paul asks us never to be a stumbling block, for the kingdom is not food and drink.
Jesus, the Good Shepherd, lays down his life freely, and will gather one flock.
2027-03-14.action: Make a definite break this week with the one thing you keep looking back at.
2027-03-14.question: What am I looking back at, and whom might my freedom cause to stumble?
catechism: The Church as sheepfold and flock.
kidsaint: She was a queen in Germany more than a thousand years ago, and she died on 14 March 968. She loved to help the poor and gave away so much that her own sons complained, and they even treated her unkindly. But Matilda forgave them, prayed for them, and they made peace again. Lesson: in a family, forgiveness is stronger than quarrels!
2027-03-14.special: Sixth Sunday of the Great Fast.
term: From the Greek skandalon, a trap or an obstacle on the road. In the Bible and in the Catechism, scandal means any word or deed that leads another person into sin. Paul asks Christians to give up even lawful things rather than cause a brother or sister to fall.

family.explain: Jesus says: I am the good shepherd. A good shepherd knows every one of his sheep by name and keeps them safe. When a wolf comes, a lazy helper runs away, but the good shepherd stays and protects the sheep, even if it costs his life. Jesus loves us like that. He gave his life for us on the Cross, and he rose again!
family.intention: We pray for our bishop and our parish priest, the shepherds of our Church.
family.ask: Ask: “How does Jesus our Shepherd take care of our family? Let each of us say one way.”

illus: A man in a parish in Wayanad stopped drinking during the Great Fast every year, and every year started again on Easter Sunday afternoon with his friends. One Lent his teenage son came home late, smelling of beer, and said: you do it too, Pachan. The father did not shout. That night he told his son that he would not drink again, not for Lent but for good, and asked him to keep him to it. Years later, at the son's wedding, there was no liquor at the reception. When a relative complained, the son said only: my father gave it up so that I would not fall. This is my thanks to him.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, we hear your voice; gather us now as your one flock. Amen.
share: But he lingered (Genesis 19:16). Where am I lingering, knowing I should leave?
Not one of all the good promises that the LORD had made had failed (Joshua 21:45). Which of God's promises has he kept in my life?
Resolve never to put a stumbling block in the way of another (Romans 14:13). Is there anything in my life that might make someone else fall?
The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep (John 10:11). How is the Good Shepherd caring for me now?
interc: For the Church, that she may be one flock under one shepherd.
For our bishops and priests, that they may lay down their lives for their people and never be hired hands.
For those who struggle with alcohol and other addictions, and for their families.
For those who linger at the door of conversion this Lent.
For unity among all the Churches of the St Thomas Christians.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son as the Good Shepherd, who lays down his life and takes it up again. Take us by the hand when we linger, keep us faithful to your promises, make us careful of our brothers and sisters, and bring us with him through his Passion to the joy of his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, at dawn the angels urge Lot to leave Sodom. But he lingered (Genesis 19:16). How often we too linger, knowing what we must leave. And the angels take him by the hand, the LORD being merciful to him, and bring him out. God's mercy does not wait for us to be brave.

They tell him: do not look back. But Lot's wife looked back, and became a pillar of salt (Genesis 19:26). She was out of the city, but her heart was still in it. Jesus says: remember Lot's wife (Luke 17:32). One week before Hosanna, what am I still looking back at?

Joshua tells Israel: not one of all the good promises of the LORD had failed; all came to pass (Joshua 21:45). And he gives them a charge: love the LORD, hold fast to him, and serve him with all your heart. God keeps every promise; let us keep faith with him.

Paul tells the Romans: the kingdom of God is not food and drink but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit (Romans 14:17). Let us not judge how others fast, and let us never be a stumbling block. If my drink or my habit makes my brother fall, love tells me to give it up.

Jesus says: I am the good shepherd; the good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep (John 10:11). No one takes his life from him; he lays it down of his own accord, and takes it up again. Next week we will see him do it.
Let us pray for our shepherds, our bishops and priests. Let us pray for the unity of all the sheep. And let us follow the voice of the Good Shepherd as he walks toward Jerusalem for us. Amen.
kids: Children, Lot was slow to leave a bad city, so the angels took him by the hand and led him out. God takes our hand too when we are slow to do good!
Jesus is our Good Shepherd. He knows each of us by name, and he loves us so much that he gave his life for us. Let us listen to his voice!

intro: Theme: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.”
Lot who lingered and was taken by the hand, the promises that never failed, the brother for whom Christ died, and the Shepherd who lays down his life of his own accord.

q: But he lingered; so the men seized him and his wife and his two daughters by the hand, the LORD being merciful to him, and they brought him out and left him outside the city.
points.apply: Make a definite break before Hosanna Sunday with the one thing you keep looking back at.

q: Not one of all the good promises that the LORD had made to the house of Israel had failed; all came to pass.
For in him every one of God's promises is a “Yes.” For this reason it is through him that we say the “Amen,” to the glory of God.
points.apply: Write down three promises God has kept in your life, and thank him for them at the family prayer.

sub: The strong and the weak in Rome.
The one for whom Christ died.
q: You shall not revile the deaf or put a stumbling block before the blind; you shall fear your God: I am the LORD.
For the kingdom of God is not food and drink but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.
points.apply: Give up for the rest of the fast one thing that might make someone close to you stumble.

q: I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I will make them lie down, says the Lord GOD.
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
points.apply: Pray each day this week for your bishop, your parish priest, and vocations from your parish.

concl: God's mercy takes us by the hand when we linger, and every one of his promises is Yes in Christ.
Let us never be a stumbling block, and let us follow the Good Shepherd who goes freely to Jerusalem to lay down his life for us.
2027-03-14.resolve: This week, break with what you keep looking back at, remove one stumbling block, and pray daily for your shepherds.
